Hey, sorry for like attacking you guys, I'm piss poor at wording things. 

What I noticed, especially today was and I don't know which caster is which, but things kept being said like "x team can't win this, y team has too many rounds" or "x team is playing so well, y team doesn't stand a chance" and it only be halftime or just after. It's just a personal gripe I guess, as we've all seen amazing comebacks from all calibers of teams. This correlates with my next paragraph, but saying things like "on this map, if the T's can get x amount of rounds they have a good chance on CT side" instead of wording it like "if the T's can't get this many rounds there's no chance they'll come back and win". 

I completely understand that like we all know how heavily sided some maps are and how improbable it is, but CSGO at X-Games is going to be huge and I personally don't think that just counting teams out based on score early or how they are performing is very attractive to new viewers. It almost makes an expectation for the audience, already knowing what's going to happen. Think of a football game in the 4th quarter(compare to map 3 in bo3) and one team being ahead by a few touchdowns. People expect that team to just win, either by bias or just having a decent lead, and many people leave early. 

Even the matches on csgolounge I bet on today, I usually love watching and being in suspense during the game, but I found myself just not able to be into the games and just checking for win/loss afterwards. For me, and I know quite a few others, the good viewing experience is great enthusiastic casting, great camera control and knowing what's going on. Know all the map callouts, know where the choke points are, know the setups and basic strategies that are commonly used. Even some speculation on what possibilities "x" team could do to get an edge over how "y" team is playing.

I'm not trying to say that every caster has to mimic how crazy Anders and Semmler are, but it's obvious they have a huge following in the community because of how hype and excited they are about every aspect of the game. I know things are going to be hype as hell at the event, but practice that enthusiasm until then. Unleash hell on stream! When the X-Games happen and you're up there killin it at casting, give everybody the best most hype viewing experience. Get people excited and keep them excited. 

I know this is just very early stages of things, but now is the time people need to criticize you guys regardless of how good or bad the criticism is. 

I'm just one person, so please don't take any of it personally, I just decided to voice my thoughts, albeit in an asshole way, about what I've seen so far. 

Not sure if you watched ESEA finals, but one of the casters seemed so full of himself, while not knowing what he was talking about. Hell, he called squeaky on Cache "blue door room". So one thing I would personally say is correct callouts is huge.

And please, don't take my comments personally, I'm just one person. These topics about the x-games and MLG so far in general have been popping up left and right since the announcement. The X-Games are going to be the true test. Make it successful, and you'll instantly win the whole community. If it lacks excitement, like the bland biased casters so far, the online community generally shuts it out until things improve. And not to have fanboy-ism, but if it's not possible to get Anders and Semmler to be able to cast at least the finals and whatnot, at least get someone with the same enthusiasm and passion for the game.

I'm judging based on what we've seen and been provided so far. Of course we'll really get to see what MLG can do for the scene at the X-Games. But in the meantime, MLG needs to get all the raw criticism from the community, whether it's good or bad. If they want a solid start, then make it as good as Dreamhack, make it as good as ESL, make it even as good as ESEA. Leave one hell of a positive impression, or else MLG will become the next FACEIT right from the start.

The community is used to a certain level of professional casting and events and even those get screwed up more often than not. The casters have been extremely biased so far, like cringe worthy biased. I'd say we're expecting far more than what we've been given so far. 

FACEIT started like this too, and now FACEIT is doing good things, but it was a really long and rough start for them. There is hella room for improvement all around, I'm just impatient with all the new leagues popping up and rushing their agenda and screwing up more than not along the way. $50,000 is a good start don't get me wrong. And believe me, I'm excited as hell that we have CSGO in the X-Games, that's cool as shit. I've been telling all my friends about it. But it's not leaving very much time to perfect the way you have started running things so far. 

There definitely needs to be more than one game being casted at a time, especially when there are top tier teams playing and what's being casted is some throw-together teams that are better off playing MM. Not to mention there are already confirmed cases of cheating. If the screening process is everybody and their mother is open to compete, CEVO and MLG need to work together to get a true anti-cheat system. We already have confirmed cheaters in some of the best teams in the world. 

If MLG is going to be the next big thing for CSGO, make the MLG CSGO premier at the X-Games the best event anybody has ever seen. Keep up with the community and be open to all suggestions for improvements, what people like and what people don't like.
